newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot may lease Boeings if Russian jets delayed.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot may lease Boeings if Russian jets delayed.

text.p: Russia's flagship carrier Aeroflot may lease a few Boeing long-range jets if Russian-made Ilyushin-96M passenger aircraft are not delivered in time, Aeroflot's acting chief executive said on Monday.
Valery Okulov told Reuters his company hoped to receive soon the first long-range Ilyushin-96M jet powered by U.S.-made engines and avionics.
"It is a promising aircraft and we are waiting for it," Okulov said. But he said if Il-96M's plane-maker delays delivery of the jets, Aeroflot may lease a few Boeing jets.
"We have kept this alternative in mind," Okulov said. He did not say what type of Boeings could be leased.
Aeroflot has ordered 17 Il-96M passenger jets and three Il-96T freighters. The first passenger craft is due to be delivered next year, and the entire order should be delivered by 2002.
Russia's Voronezh aviation plant which produces Il-96M planes has encountered financial problems and postponed several times the start of Il-96M test flights.

Last year Aeroflot-Russian International Airlines said it planned to buy 10 Boeing 737-400 passenger jets in 1997-98 to replace outdated Tupolev-134 planes on short and medium routes. The long-range Boeings would be in addition to this order.
Okulov said Aeroflot was now negotiating with Boeing about the medium-range deal.
Okulov was named acting head of Aeroflot last week after President Boris Yeltsin appointed the company's previous chief Yevgeny Shaposhnikov to his Kremlin staff.
